title: Off-policy evaluation and the final alignment audit
outcome: Evaluate a changed finite policy from logged actions with explicit propensity/support assumptions, and connect the result to an independent alignment decision.

exercises.title: Recover behavior value
exercises.task: Set the target policy equal to the behavior policy in case A.
exercises.expected: All weights are 1 and the mean observed reward is 0.75.
exercises.hint: The ratio cancels when the policies match.
exercises.answer: This is a basic estimator invariant under the constructed log.

exercises.title: Evaluate a useful target
exercises.task: Use target rows[0.9,0.1] and[0.1,0.9] with the exact synthetic outcome table.
exercises.hint: Average the target reward over the two equally weighted contexts.
exercises.answer: Known counterfactual outcomes make this value inspectable only in the authored environment; real evaluations need data and assumptions.

exercises.title: Remove behavior support
exercises.task: Give an action zero behavior probability but positive target probability.
exercises.hint: No finite importance ratio supplies an unobserved action outcome.
exercises.answer: A value model may extrapolate there, but that is a different identifying assumption and not justified by overlap-based evaluation alone.

exercises.title: Use a zero outcome model
exercises.task: Set every outcome-model prediction to zero.
exercises.expected: The doubly robust expression reduces to ordinary importance sampling.
exercises.answer: This algebraic check separates the correction structure from a claim that the supplied model is correct.

exercises.title: Interpret self-normalization
exercises.task: Compare IPS and SNIS in case B.
exercises.hint: Their denominators are n and the observed weight sum.
exercises.answer: Self-normalization changes the estimator. A useful variance tradeoff should not be described as exact finite-sample unbiasedness.

exercises.title: Audit the final claim
exercises.task: Choose a policy after inspecting many estimates from the same log.
exercises.expected: Treat that log as selection evidence and obtain a protected final assessment.
exercises.hint: The holdout rule still applies after policy optimization.
exercises.answer: A complete alignment decision needs independent task utility, support, uncertainty and critical-condition evidence, not only a favorable training reward or off-policy point estimate.
